examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Write a stack-content invariant for each input phase. Distinguish accepting by empty stack from accepting by final state, and include epsilon transitions that can remove extra symbols. One mandatory epsilon pop can change an inequality from n≤m to n<m. Deterministic PDAs recognize a strict subset of CFLs.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A PDA pushes one A per a, pops one per b, then must pop one extra A by epsilon before clearing the stack. How many a⁴bⁿ strings can it accept for integer n≥0?

**Answer: 4.** After four a's it has four A symbols. Reading n b's leaves 4−n; the compulsory epsilon pop requires 4−n≥1, so n=0,1,2,3. These give four strings.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
A stack stores unbounded nested information, but one stack does not generally support two independent crossing equalities.

One stack is enough for aⁿbⁿ but not for the general language aⁿbⁿcⁿ.
